steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A series of exercises performed one after another at different stations. Each station targets a different muscle group or fitness component, with a set time or number of reps at each station, followed by a short rest before moving to the next.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Exercising at a steady, moderate intensity for a sustained period without rest breaks. The heart rate is maintained at 60-80% of maximum heart rate throughout the session.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: "Speed play" - a form of continuous training where the intensity varies throughout the session. The performer alternates between fast and slow running (or other activities) over varying terrain, without structured rest periods.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Alternating periods of high-intensity exercise with periods of rest or low-intensity recovery. HIIT (High Intensity Interval Training) involves very intense bursts (85-95% max HR) with short recovery periods.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: For each training method, know: definition, which component it develops, advantages AND disadvantages Be ready to RECOMMEND a training method for a specific sport and JUSTIFY your choice Fartlek = "speed play" = variable pace continuous training Interval = work-rest intervals; HIIT = very intense intervals Plyometric = explosive power; Weight training = strength/endurance depending on reps Circuit training is the most versatile - it can be adapted for almost any fitness goal
